intent.raw_query: Montreal food and festivals, $1500 solo, 4 days, July 2027, from Toronto

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight AC lands at 13:00, so no morning activities scheduled. Travel from the airport to your accommodation in Old Montreal via the 747 express bus (~$11 CAD), the most budget-friendly airport transfer option.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Food Crawl: After checking in, explore the cobblestone streets of Old Montreal on foot. Stop at iconic spots for classic poutine, smoked meat sandwiches, and bagels. This self-guided wander doubles as orientation to your neighborhood and keeps costs low by grazing rather than sitting down for a full meal.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Old Port waterfront (Vieux-Port) to enjoy the warm summer evening, street performers, and free views of the St. Lawrence River. Grab a cheap BeaverTail pastry (~$7 CAD) from a kiosk as a sweet treat to end the day.

meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable smoked meat sandwich at a deli counter or food stand in Old Montreal (~$10–$14 CAD) during the food crawl.
meals.dinner: La Banquise (a Montreal institution) — open 24/7, famous for budget-friendly poutine with dozens of topping options (~$14–$18 CAD). A short metro/bus ride from Old Montreal.

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a OPUS transit card at the airport or a metro station — a single fare is ~$3.75 CAD. The 747 bus from YUL airport accepts the OPUS card. Keep luggage light for the walk to your Old Montreal accommodation. Weather should be warm (~25°C), perfect for walking.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Take the metro (Orange Line) to Jean-Talon station and spend the morning exploring one of North America's largest open-air markets. Sample local Quebec cheeses, maple products, fresh fruit, and artisan breads. Many vendors offer free tastings. Budget ~$15–$20 CAD for snacks and small purchases.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the market, head to Parc La Fontaine (free entry) in the Plateau-Mont-Royal neighborhood for a relaxing picnic with market finds. Afterward, explore the colorful murals and boutiques of the Plateau on foot — one of Montreal's most vibrant and photogenic neighborhoods at zero cost.
day_by_day.evening: St-Laurent Boulevard Street Festival Stroll: Make your way to St-Laurent (The Main) to join locals at one of Montreal's beloved neighborhood street festivals. Enjoy live music, street food vendors, and a buzzing atmosphere. Many performances are free or low-cost.

meals.breakfast: Pick up a fresh croissant and coffee at a boulangerie near Old Montreal (~$5–$7 CAD) before heading to Jean-Talon.
meals.lunch: Assemble a picnic at Jean-Talon Market — a wedge of local cheese, fresh baguette, seasonal fruit, and a small jar of Quebec maple spread (~$12–$16 CAD total).
meals.dinner: Grab budget street food along St-Laurent during the festival — options typically include grilled corn, crepes, sausages, and more (~$10–$15 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: The metro ride from Old Montreal (Champ-de-Mars) to Jean-Talon is about 25 minutes and costs one fare (~$3.75 CAD). Bring a reusable bag for market purchases. Jean-Talon Market opens around 7:00 AM — arriving by 9:00–10:00 AM means smaller crowds. Check the City of Montreal events calendar to confirm St-Laurent festival dates and free concert schedules.

day_by_day.morning: Montreal en Lumière Festival Experience: July in Montreal is packed with festivals — check if the summer edition of Montreal en Lumière or a similar culinary/cultural festival is running. Explore the festival grounds (often centered near Place des Arts or the Old Port) in the morning when it's less crowded. Many outdoor stages and exhibitions are free to access.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Mount Royal Park (Parc du Mont-Royal) — a short bus ride from downtown. Hike or walk up to the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout for a stunning panoramic view of the city skyline. The park is completely free and beloved by locals. Rent a pedal boat on Beaver Lake (~$20 CAD/hour for two) if you want a fun optional activity.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Montreal en Lumière Festival for the evening programming — outdoor concerts, light installations, and culinary showcases are often free or low-cost in the public areas. Soak in the festive summer atmosphere with locals.

meals.breakfast: Café Olimpico or a similar neighborhood café in the Plateau or Mile End — café au lait and a toasted bagel with cream cheese (~$7–$9 CAD). Montreal bagels are a must-try!
meals.lunch: Marché Atwater food stalls or a nearby food truck near Mount Royal — a hearty sandwich or bowl (~$12–$15 CAD).
meals.dinner: Festival food stalls at Montreal en Lumière offer diverse and affordable options (~$12–$18 CAD). Alternatively, try a BYOW (Bring Your Own Wine) restaurant in the Plateau for a sit-down budget-friendly dinner — many offer table d'hôte menus from ~$20–$25 CAD.

day_by_day.notes: Bus 11 from Mont-Royal metro station goes directly into Parc du Mont-Royal. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the park trails. Check the official Montreal en Lumière website for the 2027 schedule and any ticketed vs. free events. BYOW restaurants are a uniquely Montreal budget dining hack — bring a bottle of wine from a SAQ (liquor store) to save significantly on your meal cost.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Marché Bonsecours and the surrounding Old Montreal neighborhood at a leisurely pace. Visit the Notre-Dame Basilica exterior (free to admire from outside; entry fee ~$15 CAD if you choose to go inside). Browse the historic architecture of Place Jacques-Cartier, where street artists and performers gather on weekend mornings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Chinatown (a short walk or metro ride from Old Montreal) for an affordable and delicious lunch, then explore the neighborhood's colorful streets. Afterward, visit the free outdoor sections of the Quartier des Spectacles — Montreal's cultural heart — where public art installations and murals are always on display.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening back in Old Montreal — enjoy a farewell dinner at a classic Quebec restaurant. Spend any remaining time strolling the illuminated cobblestone streets of Old Montreal, which are especially atmospheric at night in summer.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh Montreal bagel and coffee from a market stall or café in Old Montreal (~$5–$8 CAD) — a perfect, cheap, and iconic Montreal morning.
meals.lunch: Chinatown lunch special — many restaurants offer weekday/weekend lunch combos with soup, main, and rice for ~$10–$14 CAD. Try a Vietnamese pho or Chinese BBQ plate.
meals.dinner: Au Pied de Cochon is iconic but pricey — instead, opt for a budget-friendly Quebec comfort food spot in Old Montreal. Look for a restaurant offering a table d'hôte with tourtière or Quebec-style lamb stew (~$20–$28 CAD including a drink).

day_by_day.notes: Saturday mornings at Place Jacques-Cartier are lively with performers and market vendors — great for people-watching at no cost. If your departure flight is on July 19, confirm check-out time with your accommodation and store luggage at the hotel if needed. The 747 bus back to YUL airport runs 24/7. Total estimated daily spend for Day 4: ~$40–$60 CAD including transport, meals, and optional entry fees.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Montreal-Trudeau Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Old Montreal Stay hotel, check in, freshen up, and get oriented with a leisurely walk along the cobblestone streets of Old Montreal to shake off travel fatigue.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Food Crawl: Wander the historic cobblestone streets of Old Montreal starting around 14:30. Stop at iconic spots for classic poutine, smoked meat sandwiches, and local Quebec treats. This is the perfect introduction to the city since it departs directly from your hotel neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Old Port waterfront at dusk, enjoy the lively summer atmosphere, and catch any outdoor street performers or pop-up events near Place Jacques-Cartier. End the evening with a relaxed dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: N/A — mid-flight or airport snack on arrival day
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at a café near the hotel shortly after check-in — try Olive & Gourmando on Rue Saint-Paul for a sandwich and coffee (mid-range, ~$18–22 CAD)
meals.dinner: Dinette Triple Crown on Rue Notre-Dame Ouest for Southern-inspired comfort food with a Quebec twist — hearty portions, craft beer, mid-range (~$30–40 CAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight lands at 13:00, allow roughly 1.5–2 hours for baggage, customs, and transit to Old Montreal. Keep Day 1 light and local — everything is walkable from the hotel. Wear comfortable shoes for the cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Mile End Bagel and Brunch Experience: Head to the bohemian Mile End neighborhood (15–20 min by metro or Bixi bike). Visit the legendary Fairmount or St-Viateur bagel bakeries for fresh wood-fired bagels straight out of the oven. Explore the artsy streets, browse independent boutiques, and soak up the neighborhood's creative energy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Continue north to Jean-Talon Market (a short metro ride from Mile End), one of North America's largest open-air markets. Sample local Quebec cheeses, maple products, fresh berries, charcuterie, and artisan preserves. Chat with vendors, pick up snacks for later, and immerse yourself in authentic Quebec food culture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Plateau-Mont-Royal area for dinner, then explore the lively terrasses (outdoor patios) along Avenue Mont-Royal — a quintessential Montreal summer evening experience with locals out in full force.

meals.breakfast: Fairmount Bagel in Mile End — fresh bagels with cream cheese and lox (~$8–12 CAD) — an iconic Montreal must-do
meals.lunch: Graze on samples and small bites at Jean-Talon Market — cheese, cured meats, fresh fruit, and a crêpe from a market vendor (~$15–20 CAD)
meals.dinner: L'Express on Rue Saint-Denis — a beloved classic French bistro with moules-frites, steak tartare, and excellent house wine. Mid-range (~$35–45 CAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: July is peak market season at Jean-Talon — arrive before 14:00 for the best selection and fewer crowds. Bring a small tote bag for market finds. Bixi bike-share is a fun and affordable way to travel between Mile End and Jean-Talon.

day_by_day.morning: Montreal en Lumière Festival Experience (summer edition): Check the festival schedule for morning or midday culinary events, outdoor tastings, or chef demonstrations happening around the city. Montreal's summer festival season is in full swing in July — even if the main festival dates vary, the city hosts numerous related food and culture events. Start the day by exploring any festival activations near the Quartier des Spectacles.
day_by_day.afternoon: St-Laurent Boulevard Street Festival Stroll: Join locals along 'The Main' (Boulevard Saint-Laurent) for one of Montreal's many neighborhood street festivals. Browse food stalls, live music stages, local artisan vendors, and street performers. This is peak Montreal summer culture — vibrant, multicultural, and completely free to enjoy.
day_by_day.evening: Stay on or near Saint-Laurent for the evening as the street festival atmosphere peaks after sunset. Enjoy live music, outdoor bars, and the electric energy of a Montreal Friday night in summer.

meals.breakfast: Café Olimpico on Rue Saint-Viateur in Mile End — a legendary espresso bar with pastries, beloved by locals for decades (~$10–14 CAD)
meals.lunch: Festival food stalls along Saint-Laurent Boulevard — try a smoked meat sandwich from Schwartz's Deli (a Montreal institution, ~$18–22 CAD) just steps from the festival route
meals.dinner: Buvette Chez Simone on Avenue du Parc — a buzzy wine bar with excellent small plates, charcuterie boards, and Quebec cheeses. Perfect for a festive Friday evening (~$35–45 CAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Friday evenings on Saint-Laurent are especially lively in July. Check the Montreal en Lumière and Just for Laughs festival websites ahead of time for any ticketed evening events worth booking. Weather forecast shows warm and mostly dry — ideal for outdoor festival strolling.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning in Old Montreal — revisit any favorite spots from Day 1 or explore the Marché Bonsecours and the historic Notre-Dame Basilica (book tickets in advance for the Aura light show if interested). Take a slow walk along the Old Port and enjoy a final Quebec breakfast at a terrace café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Mont Royal Park — take the metro to the base of the mountain and hike or walk up to the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout for a panoramic view of the entire city. Rent a Bixi bike for a scenic ride around the mountain. Stop at Lac des Castors (Beaver Lake) for a relaxing break before heading back down.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner celebration in Old Montreal near the hotel — choose a special restaurant to close out the trip on a high note, reflecting on four days of incredible food and festival culture.

meals.breakfast: Crew Café or Titanic on Rue Saint-Pierre in Old Montreal — excellent brunch with eggs Benedict, fresh juice, and locally roasted coffee (~$18–25 CAD)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch assembled from Old Montreal delis and bakeries — grab a baguette, local cheese, charcuterie, and fruit for a scenic picnic at Mont Royal Park (~$15–20 CAD)
meals.dinner: Garde Manger on Rue Saint-François-Xavier — Chef Chuck Hughes' celebrated Old Montreal restaurant known for indulgent seafood towers, lobster poutine, and a festive atmosphere. A worthy splurge to end the trip (~$55–70 CAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Mont Royal Park is free and one of Montreal's most beloved spaces — locals flock here on summer weekends with drums, picnics, and spontaneous tam-tam gatherings near the monument. If departing on Day 5, pack bags the night before and confirm any early checkout arrangements with the hotel.

Stop at iconic spots for classic poutine at Au Pied de Cochon's sister venues, smoked meat tastings, artisanal cheeses, and locally sourced charcuterie. The tour weaves through Place Jacques-Cartier and the waterfront, giving you an immersive first taste of Québécois culinary culture.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll along the Old Port waterfront, followed by a reservation at Toqué! — one of Montreal's most celebrated fine-dining institutions. Enjoy a seasonal tasting menu highlighting local Quebec ingredients, paired with a curated wine selection from their award-winning cellar.

meals.lunch: Light bites and tastings during the Old Montreal Food Crawl (poutine, smoked meat, local cheeses, and artisan bread included in the experience)
meals.dinner: Toqué! — Signature tasting menu with wine pairing; reserve the chef's table for an exclusive kitchen-view experience

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private luxury transfer from the airport. Confirm hotel early check-in if possible given the 13:00 arrival. Toqué! reservations should be booked well in advance — request the chef's table when reserving. Comfortable walking shoes recommended for cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Mile End Bagel and Brunch Experience: Head to the bohemian Mile End neighborhood for a leisurely morning. Begin at the legendary Fairmount Bagel bakery — open 24 hours and wood-fired — to watch bakers craft iconic Montreal bagels. Then wander to St-Viateur for a second tasting and comparison. Explore the neighborhood's indie boutiques and vibrant street murals before settling into a premium brunch at Café Sardine or Lawrence Restaurant, known for their elevated farm-to-table weekend spreads.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Journey to one of North America's largest and most celebrated open-air markets. A private guide leads you through stalls sampling Quebec artisanal cheeses, maple products, fresh fruit, heritage-breed meats, and locally grown vegetables. Meet the producers, learn about Quebec's agricultural heritage, and select premium provisions. Optionally visit a nearby specialty épicerie for curated Quebec spirits and ice ciders to bring back to the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: St-Laurent Boulevard Street Festival Stroll: As dusk falls, join the electric atmosphere along 'The Main' during one of Montreal's beloved neighborhood street festivals. Live music, local vendors, and an authentic local crowd fill the boulevard. Cap the night with dinner at Monarque in Old Montreal — an elegant brasserie with a locally sourced seasonal menu and exceptional natural wine list.

meals.breakfast: Freshly baked Montreal bagels with house-made cream cheese and smoked salmon at Fairmount Bagel, paired with a specialty coffee from a nearby café
meals.lunch: Elevated brunch at Lawrence Restaurant in Mile End — charcuterie boards, seasonal egg dishes, and house-baked pastries
meals.dinner: Monarque Brasserie — refined Québécois cuisine with a focus on local producers; try the duck confit or seasonal fish with a curated natural wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is liveliest mid-morning to early afternoon — arrive by 10:30 AM for the best selection. Book a private market guide for a more curated luxury experience. St-Laurent festival dates should be confirmed in advance as specific street festival schedules vary by block and week. Bring a small tote bag for market purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Montreal en Lumière Festival Experience (Summer Edition): Immerse yourself in Montreal's celebrated festival scene. The summer programming features world-class culinary events, outdoor performances, and exclusive chef collaborations across the city. Begin with a ticketed morning masterclass or tasting event — options often include a Quebec cheese and wine pairing workshop or a maple-forward cooking demonstration led by a celebrated local chef. Check the festival program for VIP access options.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Plateau-Mont-Royal at your own pace: Visit the vibrant Plateau neighborhood, strolling along Rue Rachel and Parc Lafontaine. Browse independent boutiques, galleries, and design shops. Stop for a leisurely café au lait and a pastry at a neighborhood terrasse. For the adventurous, rent electric bikes for a scenic ride around Parc Lafontaine and up to the Kondiaronk Belvedere on Mont Royal for panoramic city views.
day_by_day.evening: Premium festival dining experience: Leverage the Montreal en Lumière festival's signature restaurant takeovers or collaborative dinners, where visiting Michelin-starred chefs partner with local Montreal restaurants for one-night-only menus. Alternatively, dine at Le Mousso — Chef Antonin Mousseau-Rivard's avant-garde tasting menu restaurant — for one of the most innovative and prestigious dining experiences in Canada, followed by cocktails at the rooftop bar of Hotel William Gray overlooking Old Montreal.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at your Old Montreal luxury property — request a curated continental spread with local Quebec cheeses, smoked salmon, and fresh pastries delivered to your room or enjoyed on a private terrace
meals.lunch: Casual but elevated terrasse lunch in Plateau-Mont-Royal — try Pastel for modern Québécois small plates and natural wines in a chic, airy setting
meals.dinner: Le Mousso — multi-course avant-garde tasting menu with beverage pairing; one of Canada's most acclaimed dining experiences. Book 6–8 weeks in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Montreal en Lumière summer programming should be verified closer to the travel date — VIP and chef's table tickets sell out quickly. Hotel concierge can assist with securing festival reservations. Hotel William Gray rooftop is open to non-guests but can be busy on weekends — arrive early or have the concierge arrange a reserved spot.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Old Montreal: Sleep in and enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast. Take a private guided walking tour of Old Montreal's historic architecture — including Notre-Dame Basilica (book a Grand Organ concert or private illuminated evening tour if returning), Pointe-à-Callière Museum, and the old fortification walls. The warm July morning is perfect for lingering in the cobblestone laneways with an espresso from Crew Collective & Café, housed in a stunning former banking hall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell culinary experience — return to the Jean-Talon or Atwater Market area for a final curated shopping stop to bring home premium Quebec souvenirs: aged cheddar, maple syrup, ice cider, and locally crafted spirits. Then enjoy a long, leisurely farewell lunch at Joe Beef or Liverpool House in Little Burgundy — Montreal's most iconic and beloved fine-dining destination, famous for its indulgent, market-driven menu and legendary wine cellar.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening at leisure in Old Montreal: Enjoy a cocktail on the terrace of your hotel or at a nearby rooftop bar overlooking the St. Lawrence River. For a memorable closing dinner, reserve a table at Maison Boulud inside the Ritz-Carlton Montreal — Chef Daniel Boulud's elegant Montreal outpost offering refined French-inspired cuisine with Quebec seasonal ingredients, impeccable service, and a world-class wine program.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent in-room or terrace breakfast at the hotel — smoked salmon, Quebec cheeses, fresh croissants, seasonal fruit, and specialty coffee or champagne to celebrate the final morning
meals.lunch: Joe Beef or Liverpool House in Little Burgundy — legendary Montreal institution; the prix-fixe lunch is a rare treat featuring chalkboard specials, fresh oysters, and decadent seasonal mains with an extraordinary wine list
meals.dinner: Maison Boulud at the Ritz-Carlton Montreal — refined French-Québécois tasting menu with sommelier-guided wine pairing; request a garden terrace table for a magical summer evening farewell

day_by_day.notes: Joe Beef lunch service is extremely popular — reserve as early as possible, ideally weeks ahead. Maison Boulud at the Ritz is ideal for a celebratory farewell dinner with impeccable service. If departing early the next morning, arrange a hotel late checkout or luggage storage. Ask the concierge to organize a private car or luxury transfer for any onward travel. Notre-Dame Basilica's AURA immersive light show is a stunning optional evening add-on if time permits.
